headline: Approved four bundled tax refunds unanimously and advanced a police facility dog order 12-2.
summary: Council members asked about the purpose of the facility dog, its costs to the town, and how it would operate. Two people spoke during public comment, and the council heard several committee and liaison reports. The dog order returns to the full Legislative Council for final consideration at a later meeting.
decisions: Approved four bundled tax refunds, including $6883.29 and $17,216.30, unanimously.
Advanced the order to accept a facility dog for the police department 12-2; the full Council will give final consideration later.

Order to accept a facility dog from Puppies Behind Bars, Inc. for the Hamden Police Department
plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, 
CONNECTICUT 
 
LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL 
WORKSHOP MEETING  
7:00 PM, OCTOBER 26, 2026 
 
MINUTES DRAFT 
 
Present - Katie Kiely, President 
 Present - Sean Cardwell, Pro Tem 
Present - Sarah Gallagher, Maj Leader 
Bob Anthony, Min Leader 
Present - Tasha Hunt, Majority Whip 
Present - Tom Figlar, Minority Whip 
Present - Maurine Crouch 
Present - Doug Foley 
Present - Jeron Alston 
Present - Abdul Osmanu 
Present - Rhonda Caldwell 
Present - Grace Teodosio 
Present -Adrian Webber 
Present - Ted Stevens 
Present - Tameeka Parks  
1. CALL OF THE MEETNG AND TAKING OF THE ROLL 
Legislative Council Meeting, October 26, 2026 – 7:00pm.  President Kiely called the 
meeting to order at 7:04 with the members noted above in attendance.  Minority Leader 
Anthony was absent.   
 
Leadership Update and Mayor’s Report 
President Kiely deferred the Leadership Update and Mayor’s Report to the upcoming 
special meeting taking place on Wednesday, October 28th. 
 
News and Announcements 
President Kiely shared the Fire Department’s Halloween Safety Tips flyer, the Town 
Clerk’s upcoming Hamden Through Time events and she mentioned the ability to still add 
something to the Hamden Time Capsule.  She noted that more details would be shared in 
the Special Meeting on Wednesday, October 28th.event  
 
 
2. REPORT OF DEPARTMENTS, BOARDS, COMMISSIONS, AND COUNCIL LIAISONS 
  
 
Report of Audit Committee –  
Majority Leader Gallagher talked about the Audit Committee meeting that took place on 
Wednesday, October 21st and noted at its next meeting that the Committee plans to hear 
from representatives of Hartford, Waterbury, and West Haven regarding their experiences 
working with the State to obtain assistance.  
 
Report of School Building Committee –  
President Kiely reported on the School Building Committee's organizational meeting, 
chaired by Councilwoman Tameeka Parks, and provided an overview of its membership 
and responsibilities. 
 
Special Education Review –  
President Kiely also provided an update on the Board of Education's request for funding 
for a special education review.  
  
  
3.  PUBLIC COMMENT 
The Public Comment session was opened at 7:23pm.  Two individuals came forward to 
give public comment.  The Public Comment session was closed at 7;27pm.
4. CORRESPONDENCE ITEMS 
President Kiely mentioned there were two items of written correspondence received and 
noted one item was not going to be published due to the use of profanity.  
  
5. LEGISLATIVE SUBMISSION AND COMMITTEE REFERRAL ITEMS 
President Kiely reviewed some recent items that have been submitted to the Submission 
Calendar.    
  
6. REGULAR AGENDA DELIBERATION AND ACTION  
 
 1. Refund of Motor Vehicle Taxes collected between 7/1/2026 and 6/30/2027 - 
$6883.29 
      
 2. Refund of Property and Motor Vehicle Taxes collected prior to 7/1/2026 - 
$17,216.30 
      
 3. Refund of Motor Vehicle Taxes collected between 7/1/2026 and 6/30/2027 for 
Veterans - $988.42 
      
 4. Refund of Property Taxes collected between 7/1/2026 and 6/30/2027 - $4,162.52 
 
President Kiely called for a motion to open item 6.1.   
Motion: Figlar 
Second: Alston.   
 
President Kiely then called for a motion to bundle items 1-4.   
Motion: Figlar 
Second: Cardwell  
Vote: All in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions. Motion to bundle passed unanimously. 
 
President Kiely called for the vote to pass the bundled items. 
Motion: Figlar 
Second: Cardwell 
Vote: all in favor, 0 opposed, 0 abstentions.  The Items passed unanimously. 
 
***************** 
President Kiely requested Councilman Webber’s permission to bring the Order 
Accepting a Facility Dog from Puppies Behind Bars, Inc. for the Hamden Police 
Department before the full Council for discussion and review of the supporting 
documents. Councilman Webber agreed. 
 
ORDER TO ACCEPT A FACILITY DOG FROM PUPPIES BEHIND BARS, INC. 
HAMDEN POLICE DEPARTMENT 
 
President Kiely called for a motion to open the item.  
Motion: Gallagher 
Second: Webber
A lengthy discussion followed, during which several Council members raised questions 
regarding the proposed program, its intended use, any associated costs for the town, 
and operational considerations. 
 
At the conclusion of the discussion, President Kiely asked for a vote to move the item 
forward. Acting as Committee of the Whole and with no objection from the Public 
Safety Committee Chair, a motion was made: 
Motion: Cardwell 
Second: Figlar   
Vote: 12 in favor, 2 opposed (Osmanu/Crouch) and 0 abstentions.  The item passed. 
 
The item will return to the full Legislative Council for final consideration at a subsequent 
meeting.  
      
7. RECESS FOR STANDING COMMITTEE MEETINGS 
No Committees were scheduled to meet this evening, so there wasn’t a need to recess the 
Council meeting. 
 
8. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MINUTES 
There were no minutes for approval for this evening’s meeting. 
 
9. UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
There was no unfinished business for this evening’s meeting. 
 
10. NEW BUSINESS 
There was no new business for this evening’s meeting. 
 
11. ADJOURNMENT  
Motion to adjourn was made by Council member Figlar and seconded by Council member 
Foley.  President Kiely, with no objections, adjourned the meeting at 8:31pm.
